objects.definition: typedef enum { JSMN_UNDEFINED = 0, JSMN_OBJECT = 1, JSMN_ARRAY = 2, JSMN_STRING = 3, JSMN_PRIMITIVE = 4 } jsmntype_t;
objects.description: Enumeration of JSON token types recognized by jsmn: undefined, object, array, string, and primitive (number, boolean, null). Used as the type field within tokens.
Enumeration of parser error codes returned by parsing functions: out-of-tokens, invalid input, or incomplete JSON.
Token describing a JSON element parsed from the input: its type, start/end byte offsets in the JSON string, child count (size), and optionally a parent index if JSMN_PARENT_LINKS is enabled.

Parser state object maintaining the current scan position, the next token index to allocate, and the current enclosing container index. Must be initialized with jsmn_init before use and then passed to jsmn_parse.

functions.name: jsmn_init
functions.description: Initializes a jsmn_parser instance for parsing. This resets the parser’s internal position and state so it can parse a JSON string and populate tokens via jsmn_parse. Typical usage is to declare a jsmn_parser on the stack and call jsmn_init(&parser) before the first jsmn_parse call (and again to reuse the parser for a new JSON input).
requirements: parser must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid jsmn_parser storage location.
Call this before the first use of the parser with jsmn_parse, or to reset the parser before parsing a new, unrelated JSON document.

functions.name: jsmn_parse
functions.signature: JSMN_API int jsmn_parse(jsmn_parser *parser, const char *js, const size_t len, jsmntok_t *tokens, const unsigned int num_tokens);
functions.description: Parses the JSON data in js (length len) using the state in parser and writes token descriptors into the tokens array. Returns the number of tokens parsed on success, or a negative jsmnerr code on failure (JSMN_ERROR_NOMEM, JSMN_ERROR_INVAL, JSMN_ERROR_PART). If tokens is NULL, no tokens are written and the function effectively counts/validates tokens, which can be used to determine the required array size. Tokens reference ranges in the input by start/end byte offsets.
requirements: parser must be non-NULL and initialized with jsmn_init before parsing a JSON document.
js must be a non-NULL pointer to a readable buffer of at least len bytes. If a NUL byte occurs before len, parsing stops at that byte.
len must be the intended number of bytes to consider from js (the function does not require js to be NUL-terminated).
If tokens is not NULL, it must point to an array of at least num_tokens elements of type jsmntok_t; insufficient capacity causes return JSMN_ERROR_NOMEM.
If tokens is NULL, no tokens are written and num_tokens is ignored; the return value is the number of tokens that would have been produced (or a negative error).
Caller must handle negative return values: JSMN_ERROR_NOMEM (-1), JSMN_ERROR_INVAL (-2), JSMN_ERROR_PART (-3).
On success, the non-negative return value is the number of tokens parsed; only that many entries in tokens are valid.
The same parser instance maintains internal position; to parse a new, independent JSON input from the beginning, reinitialize with jsmn_init.

data_types.description: Text data intended to represent a JSON document. May include objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, and null. The buffer can contain arbitrary bytes, and parsers may handle partial or invalid JSON as error cases; however, the intended format is a JSON-encoded string.
